items.title: RFC4180 CSV parser
items.prompt:
Implement parseCsv in src/csv.mjs so that `npm test` passes. The tests define the required quoting, escaping, newline, and CRLF behavior. Do not modify anything under test/. Run the test suite after implementing and report the exact command and final result.

Work in the current directory. Write only implementation files; do not modify anything under test/.

tests.test/csv.test.mjs:
import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { parseCsv } from '../src/csv.mjs'

test('simple rows', () => assert.deepEqual(parseCsv('a,b\n1,2'), [['a', 'b'], ['1', '2']]))
test('quoted comma', () => assert.deepEqual(parseCsv('a,"b,c"\n1,2'), [['a', 'b,c'], ['1', '2']]))
test('escaped quote', () => assert.deepEqual(parseCsv('"say ""hi""",x'), [['say "hi"', 'x']]))
test('newline inside quotes', () => assert.deepEqual(parseCsv('"line1\nline2",x\n1,2'), [['line1\nline2', 'x'], ['1', '2']]))
test('crlf', () => assert.deepEqual(parseCsv('a,b\r\n1,2\r\n'), [['a', 'b'], ['1', '2']]))
test('empty fields', () => assert.deepEqual(parseCsv('a,,c\n,,'), [['a', '', 'c'], ['', '', '']]))
test('blank input', () => assert.deepEqual(parseCsv(''), []))

items.title: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901)
items.prompt: Implement `getPointer(value, pointer)` in src/pointer.mjs according to RFC 6901: empty pointer returns the root, tokens are separated by `/`, `~1` means `/` and `~0` means `~` (decode `~1` before `~0`), array indices must be canonical non-negative integers without leading zeros, and any invalid pointer, missing key, or out-of-range index must throw. Do not modify anything under test/. Run `node --test` and report the result.

tests.test/pointer.test.mjs:
import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { getPointer } from '../src/pointer.mjs'

const doc = { foo: { bar: [10, 20, { baz: 'qux' }] }, 'a/b': 1, 'm~n': 2, '': { empty: true } }

test('empty pointer returns root', () => assert.deepEqual(getPointer(doc, ''), doc))
test('nested object and array', () => assert.equal(getPointer(doc, '/foo/bar/2/baz'), 'qux'))
test('escaped slash', () => assert.equal(getPointer(doc, '/a~1b'), 1))
test('escaped tilde', () => assert.equal(getPointer(doc, '/m~0n'), 2))
test('empty key', () => assert.deepEqual(getPointer(doc, '/'), { empty: true }))
test('missing key throws', () => assert.throws(() => getPointer(doc, '/nope')))
test('array out of range throws', () => assert.throws(() => getPointer(doc, '/foo/bar/3')))
test('non numeric array index throws', () => assert.throws(() => getPointer(doc, '/foo/bar/x')))
test('leading zero array index throws', () => assert.throws(() => getPointer(doc, '/foo/bar/01')))
test('invalid pointer throws', () => assert.throws(() => getPointer(doc, 'foo')))
test('dash array token throws for get', () => assert.throws(() => getPointer(doc, '/foo/bar/-')))
test('tilde decodes in the right order', () => assert.equal(getPointer({ '~1': 5 }, '/~01'), 5))

items.title: SemVer precedence
items.prompt: Implement `compareVersions(a, b)` in src/semver.mjs returning -1, 0, or 1 using SemVer precedence: numeric major/minor/patch, prerelease ordering (release > prerelease, numeric identifiers compare numerically, numeric < alphanumeric, fewer fields < more when the prefix matches), and build metadata ignored. Invalid versions must throw. Do not modify anything under test/. Run `node --test` and report the result.

tests.test/semver.test.mjs:
import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { compareVersions } from '../src/semver.mjs'

test('equal', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.2.3', '1.2.3'), 0))
test('patch order', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.2.3', '1.2.4'), -1))
test('minor order', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.10.0', '1.9.0'), 1))
test('major order', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('2.0.0', '1.99.99'), 1))
test('release beats prerelease', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.0.0', '1.0.0-alpha'), 1))
test('numeric prerelease identifiers', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.0.0-alpha.2', '1.0.0-alpha.10'), -1))
test('numeric is lower than alphanumeric', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.0.0-1', '1.0.0-alpha'), -1))
test('fewer prerelease fields are lower', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.0.0-alpha', '1.0.0-alpha.1'), -1))
test('build metadata is ignored', () => assert.equal(compareVersions('1.0.0+build.1', '1.0.0+build.2'), 0))
test('invalid version throws', () => assert.throws(() => compareVersions('1.0', '1.0.0')))
test('invalid characters throw', () => assert.throws(() => compareVersions('1.0.0-alpha_1', '1.0.0')))

items.title: Inclusive interval merge
items.prompt: Implement `mergeIntervals(intervals)` in src/intervals.mjs. Bounds are inclusive integers; intervals overlap or touch when `start <= previousEnd + 1`. Sort the result by start. Reject non-integer bounds and `start > end` with an error. Do not mutate the input. Do not modify anything under test/. Run `node --test` and report the result.

tests.test/intervals.test.mjs:
import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { mergeIntervals } from '../src/intervals.mjs'

test('empty input', () => assert.deepEqual(mergeIntervals([]), []))
test('single interval', () => assert.deepEqual(mergeIntervals([[1, 3]]), [[1, 3]]))
test('overlapping intervals', () => assert.deepEqual(mergeIntervals([[1, 3], [2, 5]]), [[1, 5]]))
test('adjacent inclusive intervals merge', () => assert.deepEqual(mergeIntervals([[1, 3], [4, 5]]), [[1, 5]]))
test('nested interval', () => assert.deepEqual(mergeIntervals([[1, 10], [2, 3]]), [[1, 10]]))
test('unsorted input', () => assert.deepEqual(mergeIntervals([[6, 8], [1, 3], [2, 4]]), [[1, 4], [6, 8]]))
test('disjoint intervals stay separate', () => assert.deepEqual(mergeIntervals([[1, 2], [4, 5]]), [[1, 2], [4, 5]]))
test('non integer bounds throw', () => assert.throws(() => mergeIntervals([[1.5, 2]])))
test('reversed bounds throw', () => assert.throws(() => mergeIntervals([[5, 2]])))
test('input is not mutated', () => {
  const input = [[6, 8], [1, 3], [2, 4]]
  const copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(input))
  mergeIntervals(input)
  assert.deepEqual(input, copy)
})

items.title: Deterministic topological sort
items.prompt: Implement `topoSort(nodes, edges)` in src/topo.mjs using Kahn's algorithm with lexicographic tie-breaking at every step, so the result is deterministic. Throw on duplicate nodes, edges naming unknown nodes, malformed edges, and cycles. Do not modify anything under test/. Run `node --test` and report the result.

tests.test/topo.test.mjs:
import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { topoSort } from '../src/topo.mjs'

test('chain', () => assert.deepEqual(topoSort(['a', 'b', 'c'], [['a', 'b'], ['b', 'c']]), ['a', 'b', 'c']))
test('lexicographic tie break', () => assert.deepEqual(topoSort(['b', 'a', 'c'], []), ['a', 'b', 'c']))
test('diamond is deterministic', () => assert.deepEqual(topoSort(['d', 'b', 'c', 'a'], [['a', 'b'], ['a', 'c'], ['b', 'd'], ['c', 'd']]), ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']))
test('cycle throws', () => assert.throws(() => topoSort(['a', 'b'], [['a', 'b'], ['b', 'a']])))
test('self cycle throws', () => assert.throws(() => topoSort(['a'], [['a', 'a']])))
test('unknown node throws', () => assert.throws(() => topoSort(['a'], [['a', 'z']])))
test('duplicate node throws', () => assert.throws(() => topoSort(['a', 'a'], [])))
test('disconnected nodes are sorted', () => assert.deepEqual(topoSort(['z', 'x', 'y'], []), ['x', 'y', 'z']))

items.title: JSON Patch (RFC 6902)
items.prompt: Implement `applyPatch(document, operations)` in src/jsonpatch.mjs for RFC 6902 add/remove/replace/test operations using RFC 6901 JSON Pointers. Operations must be applied in order; a failing test operation must throw and leave the input document unmodified. Support array add (including `-` append), remove, replace, nested objects, and `~0`/`~1` escaping. Do not modify anything under test/. Run `node --test` and report the result.

tests.test/jsonpatch.test.mjs:
import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { applyPatch } from '../src/jsonpatch.mjs'

const base = { a: { b: [1, 2, 3] }, 'x/y': 1, 'm~n': 2 }
test('replace nested value', () => assert.deepEqual(applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'replace', path: '/a/b/1', value: 9 }]).a.b, [1, 9, 3]))
test('add object key', () => assert.equal(applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'add', path: '/a/c', value: 4 }]).a.c, 4))
test('array append with dash', () => assert.deepEqual(applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'add', path: '/a/b/-', value: 4 }]).a.b, [1, 2, 3, 4]))
test('array insert at index', () => assert.deepEqual(applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'add', path: '/a/b/1', value: 8 }]).a.b, [1, 8, 2, 3]))
test('remove array element', () => assert.deepEqual(applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'remove', path: '/a/b/0' }]).a.b, [2, 3]))
test('remove object key', () => assert.equal('x/y' in applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'remove', path: '/x~1y' }]), false))
test('escaped tilde', () => assert.equal(applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'replace', path: '/m~0n', value: 5 }])['m~n'], 5))
test('test passes then replace', () => assert.equal(applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'test', path: '/a/b/0', value: 1 }, { op: 'replace', path: '/a/b/0', value: 7 }]).a.b[0], 7))
test('failed test throws', () => assert.throws(() => applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'test', path: '/a/b/0', value: 2 }])))
test('missing path throws', () => assert.throws(() => applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'replace', path: '/missing', value: 1 }])))
test('remove missing throws', () => assert.throws(() => applyPatch(base, [{ op: 'remove', path: '/a/nope' }])))
test('input is not mutated on failure', () => {
  const source = { a: [1] }
  assert.throws(() => applyPatch(source, [{ op: 'add', path: '/a/-', value: 2 }, { op: 'test', path: '/a/0', value: 9 }]))
  assert.deepEqual(source, { a: [1] })
})
test('non array operations throws', () => assert.throws(() => applyPatch(base, {})))
